info.name: Expense Tracker API v1
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Expense Tracker API, as a journey you can run, with the responses the API actually returned saved as examples under each request.

**Set up**

1. Import this collection and one of the environments beside it (`local` for the Docker stack on your machine, `hosted` for the live server).
2. In the environment, set `username` and `password` to an account you were given.
3. Select the environment, then run folder **0 · Start here**. It logs in and stores the tokens every other request uses.

**Run everything**

Open the Collection Runner, untick folder **9** (it needs links from emails, and it deletes an account), and run. Folders 0 to 8 create their own data, carry ids from one request to the next in collection variables, and check every status code.

**Read**

Each request's description says what it is for and what can go wrong; its saved examples show the real response for success and for each error. The business rules behind them are in `docs/frontend/BRD.md`, and the conventions (tokens, errors, pagination, formats) in `docs/frontend/API_GUIDE.md`.

*Generated by `python manage.py build_api_docs`. Do not edit by hand: regenerate it.*

item.name: 0 · Start here
item.description: Check the server, sign in, read the profile. Run this folder first: it stores the access and refresh tokens every later request uses.

request.description: Whether the server is up and can reach its database. No sign-in needed. Answers 503 with `unavailable` when the database cannot be reached.

Exchange a username and password for an **access** token (sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access>`, valid 30 minutes) and a **refresh** token (valid 14 days, traded at `auth/refresh/` for a new pair). The response also carries the profile, including `self_participant`: the id that stands for this user in splits.

Ten failed attempts for one username from one address lock it for 15 minutes: 429 `rate_limited`.

response.name: 200 OK
Email not verified yet (403 Forbidden)

request.description: An alternative to the step above: `credential` is the ID token Google Identity Services returns from its own button. The server verifies it with Google, then finds or creates the account by its (Google-verified) email and answers exactly like a plain login -- a token pair, or `{mfa_required: true, mfa_ticket}` for an account with two-step sign-in on. `404` when the server has no `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` configured -- the feature does not exist at all until then, and the button is not shown.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: The signed-in user. Call it when the app starts, to check that a stored token still works.
Only `first_name` and `last_name` can change; `username` and `email` are read-only and ignored if sent.

item.description: The user's own categories. A category that still has expenses cannot be deleted (409).

request.description: Names are unique per user, ignoring case: `Food` and `food` are one category.

request.description: One category with its usage columns. Another user's id is a 404, never a 403.
PATCH changes only the fields sent.
PUT sends every writable field; for a category that is only `name`.
A throwaway category for the delete that follows.
Only a category with no expenses can be deleted. Otherwise the answer is 409 `protected`, `blocking` says what is in the way, and nothing is deleted.

response.name: Still has expenses (409 Conflict)

item.name: 2 · People
item.description: The people bills are split with. The list includes the user themself, marked `is_self`, which can be neither renamed nor deleted.

request.description: Someone bills are split with. People are private to each user, and names are unique per user, ignoring case.

response.name: Name already used (400 Bad Request)

request.description: A second person, for the itemised bill in folder 3.

Alphabetical, **including the user themself** with `is_self: true`: the People screen hides that row, and the expense form needs its id. `shared_count` and `item_count` say how many expenses and line items name each person.
One person.
PATCH changes only the fields sent.

response.name: Renaming yourself (403 Forbidden)

request.description: PUT sends every writable field; for a person that is only `name`.
A throwaway person for the delete that follows.
Refused with 409 when the person is on a line item or paid for an expense, and with 403 for the user themself.

response.name: Removing yourself (403 Forbidden)
On a line item (409 Conflict)

request.description: The Split tab: each person's share of the lines (or of the even split) and of the misc amount. `rows` is empty when `is_balanced` is false.
Deletes the expense with its line items and shares. There is no undo.

item.name: 4 · Dashboard
item.description: The Overview screen's numbers for a period.

request.description: Total, count, average, the biggest expense, totals per category with their share of the total, and the comparison period with the percentage change (null when the earlier period had no spending). The current month when no dates are given.

item.name: 5 · Balances
item.description: Who owes whom across all expenses, settling up, and the repayment history.

request.description: `owes_you` and `you_owe`, both as positive amounts, after repayments; `gross` is before them. All time unless `start`/`end` are given.
Records a repayment of the whole outstanding amount, in whichever direction it runs: positive when they paid you, negative when you paid them. Safe to retry.
Every repayment recorded, newest first. `?participant=<id>` narrows it to one person.
One repayment.

item.name: 6 · Exports
item.description: A CSV of expenses, built in the background: request it, wait for it, download it.

request.description: Answers at once with the job, `pending`. A worker builds the CSV and emails a link. Dates default to the current month.

Poll every second or two until `status` is `complete` (then `download_url` is set) or `failed` (then `error` says why). This request repeats itself until then.

*In the Postman runner this request repeats until finished.*
The user's exports, newest first.
The CSV, as an attachment. The file name is in `Content-Disposition`.

response.name: 200 OK
response.body:
Date,Category,Amount,Note
2026-09-12,Food,900.00,Dinner with Rahul at Toit
2026-09-18,Food,1200.00,Team lunch

item.name: 7 · Bill scans
item.description: Photograph a bill; a vision model reads it in the background; the user confirms a draft expense built from what it read.

request.description:
A multipart upload with the photo in `image`: JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 5 MB. Answers at once with the scan, `pending`.

On a server using a real vision model, upload a real photo of a bill; the sample image only works with the default `fake` reader.

response.name: Not a photo (400 Bad Request)

request.description:
Poll until `status` is `done` or `failed` (then `error` says why). Scans usually take a few seconds. This request repeats itself until then.

*In the Postman runner this request repeats until finished.*
The user's scans, newest first.
The uploaded image, for showing beside the draft.

What the model read, shaped as an expense to show for correction and then send to `POST expenses/` with `bill_scan` unchanged. `category` is set only when the model's guess matches one of the user's categories. 409 when the scan is not finished, failed, or was already saved.

response.name: Still scanning (409 Conflict)

request.description: The corrected draft, sent as a normal expense. Each scan can be saved once; the scan then points at the expense.

response.name: Already saved (400 Bad Request)

item.name: 8 · Tokens and signing out
item.description: Refreshing tokens and logging out. Run last: logging out ends the session the folders above use.

request.description: Trade the refresh token for a new pair. **The old refresh token stops working at once**: store the new one. Call this when a request fails with 401 because the access token expired, then retry the request.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Revokes this device's refresh token. Other devices stay signed in. Discard both tokens on the client.

response.name: Already logged out (400 Bad Request)

item.name: 9 · Account lifecycle (run by hand)
item.description: Sign-up, email verification, password change and reset, two-step sign-in, and deleting the account. **Not part of an automated run.** Verification and reset need the `uid` and `token` from a mailed link, which you copy into the collection variables `verify_uid`/`verify_token` or `reset_uid`/`reset_token` by hand; the two-step sign-in requests need a code from an authenticator app, which you compute from the `secret` the setup request returns; and the last request deletes the account.

request.description: Creates the account **inactive** and emails a verification link to the frontend's `/verify-email/<uid>/<token>` route. The account cannot log in until the link is used.

response.name: 201 Created
Password too weak (400 Bad Request)

request.description: The frontend's `/verify-email/<uid>/<token>` page calls this with the two parts of its URL. It activates the account and signs it in: the response is the same as a login.

response.name: 200 OK
Link already used or expired (400 Bad Request)

request.description: Needs the current password. Every other device is signed out; this one gets a new token pair in the response and stays signed in.

response.name: 200 OK
Wrong current password (400 Bad Request)

request.description: Emails a link to the frontend's `/reset-password/<uid>/<token>` route. The answer is the same whether or not an account uses the address, so it reveals nothing.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: The frontend's `/reset-password/<uid>/<token>` page sends the two parts of its URL with the new password. Every device is signed out; the user then logs in.

response.name: 200 OK
Link already used or expired (400 Bad Request)

item.name: Log in with the new password

request.description: Signing in again after the reset.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Whether two-step sign-in -- an authenticator-app code asked for after the password -- is on, and how many recovery codes are left.

A fresh secret and an `otpauth://` URI to build a QR code from. The account is not protected yet -- that needs the first code confirmed below. Calling this again before confirming replaces the pending secret.

Confirms the pending device with a code from it. Returns ten recovery codes -- shown only this once, so store them somewhere safe -- and a fresh token pair: every other refresh token is revoked, the same as a password change.

request.description: With two-step sign-in on, a right password is not enough by itself: the response carries a ticket instead of tokens. Send it, and a code, to `auth/mfa/verify/`.

The ticket from the login above, plus a code -- from the authenticator app, or one of the recovery codes shown at setup. Either way the response is the token pair a plain login would have returned.

Five wrong codes for one account in 15 minutes lock it: 429 `rate_limited`. Whoever holds a ticket already knows the password, so this cannot be used to lock out someone else's account.

response.name: 200 OK
Invalid or expired ticket (400 Bad Request)

request.description: The devices this account is signed in on -- a web session, or an app holding a refresh token -- most recently seen first. An account may be signed in on two at a time (`MAX_SIGNED_IN_DEVICES`): a third sign-in signs the oldest one out, and its next `auth/refresh/` gets 401. `label` is the device's User-Agent. `current` is true only for the web session making the request; an API device cannot tell which one it is. The next request signs the other one out.

Ends that device: a web session is deleted; an API device's refresh token is revoked, so it gets 401 on its next refresh. Its current access token keeps working until it expires (up to 30 minutes). Another account's device id is 404.

response.name: Not one of your devices (404 Not Found)

request.description: Replaces the current set of ten with a fresh one. Needs a current authenticator code, not a recovery code -- otherwise spending the last one could mint ten more.
Needs the current password **and** a current code -- neither is enough on its own. Deletes the device and every recovery code, and revokes other refresh tokens.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Deletes the account and **everything in it**, irreversibly. Confirm by sending the username as `confirm`, typed by the user.

response.name: Confirmation does not match (400 Bad Request)
